turns.assessment: The simultaneous low-count errored seconds on both ends of och16, brief protection switch activity, and errors across every service using that lightpath indicate a short bidirectional line disturbance rather than an individual client failure. Unchanged receive power, OSNR, BER trend, DGD, amplifier telemetry, and channel power argue strongly against a persistent cut, loss, amplifier, WSS, or line-card failure; unchanged power particularly favors a fast SOP transient over a power excursion. The evidence does not identify which physical span was disturbed, so no element-specific repair can be committed safely.

proposals.rationale: A millisecond-scale polarization transient on a span in the S10-to-S24 direction can produce isolated errored seconds and protection switching without a sampled change in power, OSNR, DGD, or SOP rate. Disturbance of the physical cable could also affect its reverse-direction fibre, explaining O32.

The equivalent hypothesis in the S24-to-S10 direction fits the receiver errors at S10 and the service-wide impact. The available observations cannot select a particular span or distinguish which directional fibre first experienced the transient.
Brief handling of a span could disturb both fibres and create errors, but a power excursion would be more likely to leave some receive-power or channel-power evidence than was observed.
A reverse-direction power excursion is possible but is disfavored by unchanged optical power telemetry throughout the route.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
